_source: Prices and status: Google's pages ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, /models and /thinking, read on 2026-09-21. Prices are USD per 1M tokens, text, standard paid tier, and the output price includes thinking tokens. Check the page before you rely on a number.
_ratings: The ratings are estimates from the tier and Google's description, NOT measurements. Only gemini-2.5-flash was run end to end in this project. Measure a model on a step with: tests/manual/debug_flow.py --only=<step> --state=<file> --repeat=5 --real (see docs/debugging_the_flow.md).

_levels.best: the right model for this step
_levels.good: works well, a fair price for the job
_levels.ok: works, but slower, weaker or more expensive than needed
_levels.weak: likely to fail or to give poor results here
_levels.avoid: wasteful (too expensive or too slow for what the step does)

_blend: blended cost = (3 x input + 1 x output) / 4 per 1M tokens: the calls of this agent send about three times more tokens than they get back. The list is sorted by it, cheapest first.

steps.triage_specialist: Classifies the request into a small JSON. Runs first, so latency matters. Little reasoning, but it must not ask for details it does not need.
steps.project_manager: The hardest step. Builds the plan: a recursive action tree with dependencies, types and tool choice, in a strict schema. Needs real reasoning. One call per message.
steps.safety_quality_gatekeeper: Judges the plan for risk and decides if the user must confirm. Small JSON, judgement more than reasoning. One call.
steps.cognitive_worker: One call per action of the plan: answers, analyses, writes a piece. The quality of the content comes from here. The number of calls grows with the plan.
steps.mcp_operator: One or more calls per tool action. Needs reliable function calling plus a valid JSON answer.
steps.data_engineer: Cleans the output of a tool. Mechanical: precision, no creativity.
steps.draft_writer: Writes the first answer for the user from all the outputs. Writing quality and following the constraints.
steps.editor_in_chief: Polishes the draft without adding facts and sets the final status. Faithfulness more than creativity.
steps.answer_checker: Reads the user's reply to a question: an answer, a yes or a no, not an answer, or stop. Short, any language, latency matters.
steps.user_clarification: Writes a short friendly question for the user. Trivial.

cognitive_worker.calls: 1 per action of the plan (1 to 3 is usual)
cognitive_worker.note: measured with gemini-2.5-flash: about 1,270 per action

mcp_operator.calls: 1 to 3 per tool action, 0 when no tool is used
mcp_operator.note: estimate, not measured: the tool list makes the prompt longer

data_engineer.calls: 1 per tool result, 0 when no tool is used

answer_checker.calls: 1 per reply to a question of the agent, 0 otherwise

user_clarification.calls: 1 when the agent asks the user, 0 otherwise

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite
models.summary: The cheapest and fastest. Good for short, simple tasks.

triage_specialist: Fast classifier. Watch that it does not ask too much.
project_manager: Deep plans with dependencies are too much for it.
safety_quality_gatekeeper: Fine for obvious cases, shallow on risk.
mcp_operator: Tool calling is the least reliable here.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite
models.thinking: not stated in the pages read
models.summary: Google: frontier-class performance at reduced cost.

project_manager: May plan simple requests well. Test before trusting it.
safety_quality_gatekeeper: Enough judgement for a yes or no on risk.
cognitive_worker: Good content at a low price.
mcp_operator: Function calling should be fine. Test it.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite
models.summary: Google: the fastest and most cost-effective 3.5 model. Costs 20% more input and 67% more output than 3.1 Flash-Lite.

project_manager: Better than 3.1 Flash-Lite is likely, still a lite model.
mcp_operator: Function calling should be fine. Test it.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.summary: The only model tested in this project: it works on every step, but it is slow because it always thinks (3 to 14 s for triage alone).

triage_specialist: Works, slow because of the thinking.
mcp_operator: Not tested with a real tool.

models.name: Gemini 3.6 Flash
models.thinking: medium by default. Can go down to 'minimal'.
models.summary: Google: balances speed and multimodal capabilities for general tasks. Same price as 3.7 and 3.8.

triage_specialist: Overkill, unless the thinking level is set to minimal.

models.name: Gemini 3.7 Flash
models.summary: Google: previous-generation Flash for complex coding and agentic workflows. Same price as 3.6 and 3.8.

mcp_operator: Built for agentic work with tools.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
models.summary: Google: made for long-horizon software engineering, autonomous agents and complex workflows. The newest Flash, same price as 3.6 and 3.7, so prefer it.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
models.thinking: not stated in the pages read
models.summary: Google calls it the legacy Flash. It costs more than the newer 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8 Flash (also after their price change in 2027): not recommended.

triage_specialist: Costs more than newer models that do it better.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.status: deprecated, no longer available to new users
models.price_note: prompts up to 200k tokens. Above: 2.50 in, 15.00 out.
models.summary: Deep reasoning, but Google marks it as deprecated and the API refused it with this key (404: no longer available to new users). Do not use.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro (preview)
models.price_note: prompts up to 200k tokens. Above: 4.00 in, 18.00 out.
models.summary: Google: advanced intelligence for complex problem solving. A preview: it can change, and it has no free tier.

project_manager: The strongest planner, if the plan quality is the problem.
safety_quality_gatekeeper: Very careful on risk, more than needed.
mcp_operator: Top tool use, at a price.

_api_check: 'api_check' is the result of one tiny test call per model id through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (GOOGLE_URL) with the key of this project, on 2026-09-21. It proves the id works with this key, not that the model is good at a step.
